notes: The owner's page stops posting him its photographs. It was carrying them inside itself as text: on N66BA's own job the status his browser downloaded was 1.6 MB, 99.4% of it photographs, and it fetched the whole lot again every time it checked whether anything had moved. The photographs now go up as files, once, exactly as the report and the invoice already sent theirs, and his page points at them — the same job's status is 12 KB, measured, and his telephone downloads only the pictures he scrolls down to. Nothing about the page changes for him except that it opens straight away, and every link sent before today goes on working untouched. Three things were also put right on the tablet itself. The app now asks the browser to treat this shop's work as data it may not delete on its own — without that, Safari discards a site's storage after seven days of not opening it, which is one holiday and one lost inspection. When a photograph cannot go into the picture store it says so, plainly, instead of quietly carrying it inside the inspection and making the next save bigger. And a save that is not happening now puts a red bar across the bottom of the screen with an Export button on it, rather than turning one small button in the corner red and hoping somebody looks at it. There is also a lifeboat: a separate page, reached by a plain link on the Files tab, that reads the same saved inspections and prints the report, the logbook entries and the invoice with nothing else working — and it is on the tablet from now on, not fetched when it is needed. Finally, an update that cannot fetch one of its files no longer strips the tablet of the rest: one missing file used to leave nothing cached but index.html, and no AD search could be printed for weeks afterwards with nothing saying why.
validated_against: The FAA's own model search on drs.faa.gov, 23 models, Status=Current: 693 directives listed, 693 returned, 0 wrongly set aside. Perfect on every individual model. AD Toolbox's airframe lists hold 528 of the same 693 — mostly by design, since their appliance directives sit in a separate unmatched list of 581.
reliability: 196 self checks passing, 8 of them new: that the owner's page really does send its photographs as files and carries none of them itself; that a photograph which has left the page can still be found, by the name taken from the picture itself, in that inspection's own folder; that a page published before this change is still the same shape and is left alone rather than re-sent; that one publish sends each photograph once and slims the page whether or not any documents were ticked; that the browser is asked not to throw an inspection away, without the boot ever waiting on the answer; that running out of room is said out loud; that a failed save puts a bar on the screen which clears the tab strip it is sending him to, measured on the screen it is running on; and that the lifeboat is a link rather than a button. Each of the eight was checked by breaking the thing it watches and confirming it fails — a check that cannot fail is not a check. Measured end to end against N66BA/N907HR's real 84 MB backup in headless Chromium, with the upload simulated and nothing sent anywhere: snapshot 1,643,665 bytes before, 12,013 after, a 137-fold reduction, 12 photographs uploaded once, 0 base64 left, 0 photographs left unreachable, and a second publish of the same job sending nothing again. The owner's portal was then rendered from both shapes, old and new, and drew the same page both times: 12 photographs, 12 sections, identical text, no errors. The service worker was installed twice against a deliberately broken deploy: the old one cached 2 files of 11, this one caches 10.

index.source: FAA Dynamic Regulatory System, AD Final Rules

storage: The directive index no longer shares a database with jobs and photographs. It lives in Cache Storage under 'adx-1'. Any copy left in the old place is deleted on first load. This is the second half of the 30 August fix: the database that wedged that morning is now smaller and is never touched by an AD search. From 3.390.0 the app also asks for persistent storage at startup, so a tablet's inspections are not data the browser may quietly reclaim, and it watches how full the device is — warning while there is still room to write the export that gets the job off, rather than after there is not.
writer: The workbook is written by the app, not by a library. A stored zip and five XML parts, about 160 lines, so it works on a tablet in a hangar with no signal. Checked both ways: the file reads back byte-identical through the app's own reader, and opens clean in a strict spreadsheet parser.
language: Every British spelling and idiom taken out. "Aircraft" is now "aircraft" in all 86 places it appeared, and with it labour/labor, colour/color, authorisation/authorization, recognised/recognized, digitised/digitized, grey/gray, carburettor/carburetor, neighbour/neighbor, cancelled/canceled and the rest. Two idioms went with them: a "fortnight" is now a two-week window, and the legacy-directive note that told a mechanic which fortnight to look in now says which two-week issue. Nobody on a US ramp says aircraft.
portal: The owner's status page is served from the snapshot the app publishes, and that snapshot no longer contains photographs — only links to them, in the same bucket folder the report and invoice already use. The portal needed no change to read it: a photograph has always been {url: ...} and only what the url points at is different, which is why every job published before 3.390.0 still renders. Unpublishing already deleted that whole folder, so nothing is left on the open web that was not before.
